scenarioHelp.title: Scenario assumptions
scenarioHelp.bear: revenue growth −up to 8pp (minimum 2pp adjustment), FCF margin −up to 6pp (floor 0%) and WACC +2pp (terminal growth −0.5pp). Drivers: weaker execution, margin compression and more expensive capital.
scenarioHelp.base: normalized assumptions based on historical facts (revenue CAGR and normalized FCF margin), with no scenario adjustments. It's the anchor, not a point forecast.
scenarioHelp.bull: growth +up to 8pp (cap 50%), FCF margin +up to 6pp (cap 60%) and WACC −1pp (floor: terminal growth +1pp). Drivers: stronger execution, margin expansion and cheaper capital.
scenarioHelp.note: Spreads adjust to each company's historical volatility (between 2pp and the maximum shown). Each scenario's probability comes from the confidence of the evidence and the historical growth bias, not from the model's opinions.

valuationText.reverseOk: The model price requires annual revenue growth of {growth}{basis}; it is not a forecast, it is what the price already discounts.
valuationText.reverseBasis: (with an FCF margin of {margin} and a WACC of {wacc})
valuationText.reverseOutOfBounds: Reverse DCF out of range: with the base assumptions there is no annual revenue growth between −25 % and +75 % that makes the model worth the current price, so no «required growth» is published.
valuationText.reverseNotApplicable: Reverse DCF not applicable: with an FCF margin ≤ 0, growing does not add value (more revenue burns more cash), so there is no required growth.

whatToBelieve.waccPrice: To justify {price} you need a WACC of {implied} (we use {used}).
whatToBelieve.waccPriceNoUsed: To justify {price} you need a WACC of {implied}.
whatToBelieve.waccBelow: To justify {price} you'd need a WACC below {min}: the price is beyond what this DCF can give.
whatToBelieve.waccAbove: Even at a WACC of {max} the DCF gives more than {price}: the price asks very little.
whatToBelieve.waccNotAvailable: With negative cash flows there's no meaningful implied WACC.
whatToBelieve.waccConsensus: The analyst consensus ({price}) requires a WACC of {implied}.
whatToBelieve.waccConsensusBelow: The analyst consensus ({price}) would require a WACC below {min}.
whatToBelieve.waccConsensusAbove: The analyst consensus ({price}) sits below the DCF even at a WACC of {max}.
whatToBelieve.growth: Or, at our WACC, revenue growth of {required} a year in the first stage (we project {current}).
whatToBelieve.growthNoCurrent: Or, at our WACC, revenue growth of {required} a year in the first stage.
whatToBelieve.growthOut: At our WACC, not even the model's maximum growth reaches the price.
whatToBelieve.exitTitle: Terminal value with an exit multiple
whatToBelieve.exitExplain: Same DCF, but the terminal value is {multiple} times the last projected year's free cash flow instead of perpetual growth. It's a cross-check, not our fair value.
whatToBelieve.exitImplied: Reaching {price} would take a {implied}x exit on that cash flow.
whatToBelieve.explain: WACC is the return required from the investment: the lower it is, the more the future is worth. If the price needs a WACC far below ours, it's pricing in less risk or more growth than we project.
